name: Nikita Nikolaev
title: Senior Backend Software Engineer
summary: Java Software Developer with 8+ years of experience designing, building, and delivering distributed, high-throughput backend systems. Specialized in Spring Boot microservices, REST APIs, and event-driven architectures (Kafka). Experienced in leading end-to-end feature design and implementation, and in contributing to architecture decisions across the full delivery lifecycle — design, development, and testing. I also build and run my own microservices platform on Kubernetes in Google Cloud.

experience.about: Large-scale telecom subscriber-provisioning and charging platform, built as a distributed system of Spring Boot microservices. The platform is the gateway between the operator's business systems and the charging engine, translating business requests into the data structures required by the charging platform.
points: Led the design and end-to-end implementation of new features across multiple Spring Boot microservices, owning them from technical design through testing and production rollout.
Contributed to architecture and design decisions for the distributed platform — service boundaries, REST/OpenFeign API contracts (OpenAPI/Swagger), and event-driven messaging.
Designed and implemented Kafka-based event flows for asynchronous, decoupled communication between microservices, balancing business requirements with reliability and performance.
Wrote comprehensive automated tests with TestNG, JUnit, Mockito, and WireMock, reducing regressions and stabilizing releases.
Investigated, troubleshot, and solved production issues, reducing downtime and customer impact.
AI-assisted development: built custom Cursor agent skills, rules, and MCP integrations to accelerate development, code review, debugging, and log/issue investigation.

experience.about: Social network for pet owners — a platform for communication between registered users (posts, messages, images) and lost-and-found pet announcements, built on a microservices architecture.
points: Built the Java server side of a microservices-based social platform enabling user communication, media posts, and lost-and-found pet announcements.
Implemented secure authentication and authorization with JWT and request routing via Netflix Zuul API Gateway.
Developed an email-notification flow that alerted users to matching posts with approve/deny actions.
Integrated asynchronous messaging with CloudKarafka and deployed on Heroku with MongoDB Atlas and Bonsai Elasticsearch.

experience.about: E-commerce marketplace — an online shop with a wide product assortment.
points: Developed server-side services and modules, including accounting and logging.
Contributed to frontend development and provided ongoing website support and maintenance.
Planned digital communication schemes and supervised the build-out of installation projects.
Installed and configured video surveillance systems.

projects.name: Attendance Platform
projects.tagline: Employee time-tracking system — microservices on Kubernetes in Google Cloud
projects.about: Created to go deeper into cloud-native and DevOps practice: organizations track employee clock-in/out, and the system aggregates monthly hours and overtime for salary processing. Built and operated from code to cloud.
points: Spring Boot microservices (accounting/auth issuing JWTs, time tracking, AI assistant) with a schema per service in PostgreSQL, versioned with Flyway.
Multi-tenant security: the tenant in every URL is checked against the JWT, with a role hierarchy and a platform-administrator role, packaged as a shared Spring Boot auto-configuration library.
Kafka event flows with OpenAPI-generated message contracts, messages keyed per user, dead-letter topics, and malformed messages routed straight to the DLQ without retries.

AI assistant on the Claude API that turns an employee's last six months into a trend analysis emailed to the manager, with a free stub for tests, temporary failures retried and permanent ones sent to the DLQ, and no second paid call when only the email fails.
One trace id follows each request from the HTTP call through Kafka to the email (Micrometer Tracing), with structured JSON logs on GKE.
React SPA served by nginx behind a Kubernetes ingress.
Helm chart per service, deployed to Google Kubernetes Engine with TLS from cert-manager and Let's Encrypt; Docker Compose and k3s for local development.
GitOps with Argo CD on the local k3s cluster (auto-sync, pruning, self-healing); CI on GitHub Actions with an 85% test-coverage gate and images published to GitHub Container Registry.
